title: قانونا التَّفاعل الكِيميائِيّ
sourceImageAvailability: Six textbook page images (pp. 30–35) were supplied with the rebuild task and audited directly on 2026-10-24. The scans themselves are not stored in the repository (project convention); every printed element is traced in src/data/curriculum/lesson5SourceLedger.ts.

items.coverage: Printed title «قانونا التَّفاعل الكِيميائِيّ», the four objectives (know/apply Lavoisier and Proust laws), and the keyword line are reproduced verbatim in the opening step.

The «أُلاحِظُ وأستنتجُ» prompt is verbatim; the balance figure is reconstructed as SVG (source-figure-p30-balance) with the printed counts C=3, H=5, O=5, Na=1 per pan and both formula/name strips. Atom totals are computed from the formulas by the lab model.
Both «أستنتجُ» bullets are verbatim: per-element atom counts are equal on both sides, and a chemical reaction conserves element type and atom count.

The «إثراء» text on sodium hydrogen carbonate in sweets/pastries is verbatim; the two photographs are documented in a reference card (decorative in the ledger, caption «بيكربونات الصوديوم» preserved).

The apparatus list (electronic balance, CaO pieces, glass vessel, dilute HCl, tongs) is verbatim; the two-balance figure is reconstructed (source-figure-p31-scale) with 125.100 twice and no added unit.

All four printed procedure steps are reproduced; step 2 (ماذا أُلاحظُ؟) and step 4 (أقارنُ النَّتائج) carry full platform solutions restricted to source-supported observations (CaCl2 + H2O; equal readings).
Lavoisier's law statement is verbatim including «قانون مصونيّة الكتلة»; the portrait caption (Antoine Lavoisier, born 1743, died 1794) is preserved in a reference card.

The Proust heading and intro sentence are verbatim; the three-trial pile figure (10/1.56→11.56; 10/3→11.56+1.44 S; 18/1.56→11.56+8 Pb) is reconstructed as SVG (source-figure-p32-trials) and tagged as data analysis only (lead toxicity).

The before/after table (printed row 1 with 10/1.56 = 6.41, blanks elsewhere) and all five questions appear in printed order with full solutions. The final question's printed word «الكبريت» for the 8 g leftover contradicts the p.32 figure («رصاص متبقّي»); the prompt is kept verbatim with an explicit platform misprint note and is solved for lead.
Proust's law statement is verbatim; the portrait caption (Joseph Louis Proust, born in France 1754, died 1826) is preserved in a reference card.
Both «نشاط» items are kept: the Fe/S ratio table (56:32, 28:16, 7:4 = 1.75 with the ratio row left to the learner) and the 60 g Fe + 30 g S problem (52.5 g Fe reacts, 7.5 g excess, 82.5 g compound).
Both «تعلَّمتُ» bullets (Lavoisier, Proust) are reproduced verbatim as the lesson's official summary step.
Question 1 (oxygen/hydrogen masses in 18 g of water) is verbatim and solved as 16/2 = 8:1 (auto-graded numerical).
Both question-2 items keep their printed stems, options, and a–d order (correct: b for atom counts, d for total mass).

The CO2 table keeps the printed column order (32/12, 64/24, 128/48, 16/6) and the printed value 32/12 = 2.66; solutions distinguish it from the exact 2.666… (2.67 rounded) and solve branches 1–4 (1.5 g C; 26.666… g O).
